source.title_on_document: How experience moderates the impact of AI suggestions on researchers' perceptions of their ideas

supplement.holds: Appendices A to F: Table A1 (self-assessment questions), Figs. A1 to A3, Table A2 (interview guide); Figs. B1 and B2 (outcome distributions) and Tables B1 and B2 (1 vs 3 AI suggestions comparison), Tables B3 to B5 (experience moderation of each index component); Appendix C (research agenda and attitude measures); Appendix D (robustness controls, reweighting by experience); Appendix E (field heterogeneity); Appendix F (survey on disclosure).

paper_design_summary: Study 1: 310 professors in the US, Canada, and UK uploaded the title and abstract of one of their papers and were randomly assigned to receive no AI suggestion, one GPT-4 research-idea suggestion, or three suggestions; each then wrote a new research idea and rated it themselves on novelty, feasibility, and impact. The only output-scored measure is the embedding cosine similarity between the submitted idea and the AI suggestion(s). Study 2 is a qualitative interview study with 28 researchers who all received a GPT-5.2 suggestion, with no comparison group.

studies.label: Study 1 (pre-registered online experiment, research idea generation)

participants.exclusions: Incomplete responses removed after data collection; the number removed is not stated (p. 4). Similarity regression has 309 observations (Table 3, col. 1). Experience-moderation regressions have 294 observations (Table 4); the reason for the drop is not stated in the main text. 310 is short of the pre-registered target of 450.

ai_tool.how_used: A fixed prompt asked GPT-4 for one idea for a future research project based on the participant's submitted title and abstract (max 200 words); participants did not interact with the AI and saw the suggestion(s) while drafting their idea.

task.description: Draft a new research idea based on one of their recently published papers, then self-assess it.
task.duration: Mean session about 13 minutes (p. 5); Table 1 means 13.983, 11.676, 11.942 minutes by arm

eligibility.reason: Study 1 randomly assigned 310 researchers (analyzed) to AI suggestions or none, but the creativity outcomes (novelty, feasibility, impact indices) are self-assessed by the participant who wrote the idea (the paper says 'the outcome in our study was self-assessed', p. 14). The only output-scored measure is embedding similarity between the idea and the AI suggestion, which measures incorporation of AI content, not creativity or diversity across people. Study 2 is qualitative with 28 participants and no comparison group.

one_line_finding: Among 310 randomized researchers, AI suggestions raised idea similarity to the AI suggestion (beta = 6.05, SE = 1.29) but did not change self-assessed novelty (beta = -0.218, SE = 0.194, p = 0.262), feasibility, or impact on average; experience negatively moderated self-assessed novelty (interaction -0.040, SE = 0.013) and impact (p. 7 Table 3; p. 8 Table 4).
open_questions: Whether AI suggestion-idea similarity (embedding cosine similarity to the AI suggestion, scored on output) should count as an output-scored outcome under criterion 3; I coded it as not creativity or diversity.
Why Table 4 has 294 observations versus 310 in Table 3 is not explained in the main text (possibly missing experience; not stated).
Number of incomplete responses removed before the 310 is not stated, so n_randomized is unknown.
notes: Main analyses pool the 1- and 3-suggestion arms because the paper reports no notable differences between them (Appendix Tables B1, B2, not in this PDF). Arm-level means of the outcome indices are not printed in the main text; Table 1 gives arm means of covariates only. 'Enjoyed exercise' (Table 4 col. 5: AI x experience -0.033, SE 0.017, p = 0.051) is an attitude about the task, not scored on output, and is omitted from outcomes; research agenda and attitude measures sit in Appendix C. Qualitative coding of open-ended comments (Table 5, Table 6) omitted. ai_available_when_produced is 'mixed' because the control arm worked without AI while AI arms had suggestions available.
